summary: Polls the UDP socket (this+0x0) for incoming packets. Gated on the enable flag this+0xE4; when zero the function returns the flag value without touching the socket. Otherwise it builds a single-socket fd_set and loops on select() with a zero timeout. For every readable socket it calls recvfrom() into the global buffer buf (max 255 bytes), null-terminates the received data, and dispatches the packet via FilePathNameLookup with the sender address. The loop breaks when select returns -1 or 0, and the last select result (or the flag value) is returned.

local_names.this: socket wrapper object holding the SOCKET at this+0x0 and the receive-enable flag at this+0xE4
local_names.v3: socket value loaded from this+0x0 and placed into the fd_set
local_names.v4: number of bytes received by recvfrom, used to index the buffer terminator
local_names.from: sockaddr filled by recvfrom with the sender address, passed to FilePathNameLookup
local_names.fromlen: sockaddr length (initialized to 16) passed to recvfrom

operations.description: The receive loop runs only when the flag this+0xE4 is non-zero; otherwise the function returns the flag value unchanged
Initializes the poll state: fromlen set to 16, zero timeout, and a single-entry fd_set built from the socket at this+0x0
Polling loop: select(64, &readfds, 0, 0, &timeout) with zero timeout; breaks when select returns -1 or 0
Receives one packet: recvfrom(this+0x0 socket, buf, 255, 0, &from, &fromlen)
When recvfrom returns a non-error length v4, the buffer is null-terminated: buf[v4] = 0
Dispatches the received packet data via FilePathNameLookup(v4, &from) using the sender address
Returns the last select() result, or the this+0xE4 flag value when the guard failed
